title: From the Ancestral Root We Ascend (Na Thymmei Ngi Kiew)
cultural_context: Historical ballad celebrating the roots (Thymmei) of the Khasi people from the golden era of the Seven Huts to the present, from 'Ki Sur Ka Mynnor Bad Mynta' (1998).

khasi: Na thymmei u Lum Sohpetbneng ngi la mih,
Ki hynniew trep kiba sotti bad ba khuid;
Ki kpa tymmen ki la buh ka thoh ka tar
Ha ka dohnud, ha ki maw bad ki wah;
Ngi kiew na ka por sha ka por,
Khlem da pait ka snieh-jaid jong ngi;
Ka thymmei ka long ka nongrim ba skhem
Ba tei ia ka burom ka jaidbynriew.
english: From the navel peak of Lum Sohpetbneng we arose,
The Seven Huts pristine and pure;
The ancient fathers inscribed our laws
Upon human hearts, upon monoliths, and rushing waters;
We have ascended from era to era,
Our cultural lineage unbroken and whole;
The primal root is the rock-solid foundation
That builds the majesty of our nation.

khasi: Lada u dieng u duh la ka thied,
Un kyllon haba suh ka eriong;
Kumta u briew uba klet la ka thymmei,
Un sah khlem thied ha ka pyrthei;
To ngin bat ia la ka tynrai,
Ia ka ktien bad ka akor ba bha,
Ba ngin kiew kum u mawsiang
Uba neh ha man ka por.
english: If a great tree loses its taproot,
It must crash when the tempest blows;
Even so a person who forgets their roots
Shall drift without anchor in the world;
Let us cling to our ancestral root,
To our mother tongue and noble conduct,
That we may rise like the immovable crag
Enduring through all waves of time.

vocabulary.lum sohpetbneng: naval of heaven mountain (Khasi cradle of creation)
